Porting ObjFW to Windows 95

Created: 2026-11-11T15:29
With ObjFW already running on Windows 98 SE, many people would assume it also runs on Windows 95. However, this was not the case – until now.
👉 ObjFW on Windows 98 SE

For starters, Windows 95 does not ship with msvcrt, which is the default libc used by MinGW when not using the new UCRT. msvcrt is included with Windows 98 and can be installed on Windows 95, however, since I eventually want to support Win32s, for which it has never been released, I decided to port ObjFW to crtdll. While there is the convenient “-mcrtdll=crtdll” switch in MinGW, it unfortunately does not work for ObjFW: It will still pull in libgcc_s_dw2-1.dll and friends, which are linked against msvcrt.dll, so that won't work. I ended up adding a new package to pkgsrc, called mingw-w64-i686-gcc-crtdll, which will default to crtdll and also links all compiler runtimes against crtdll.dll.

With that out of the way, the porting fun begins. The first step was to port to crtdll.dll, which means not directly referencing any symbols from msvcrt and loading them lazily when available.
🌐 Commit “Add support for using crtdll on Windows”

However, I quickly noticed that this creates problems with UCRT, as I immediately got a mail about CI failing: Well, of course! This would now also try to load _wopen etc. from msvcrt.dll, even when using UCRT. So a few #ifdefs later, UCRT support was restored.
🌐 Commit “Don't load msvcrt.dll if we're compiled with UCRT”

With that, I had working support for crtdll, but it would still not start on Windows 95: TryEnterCriticalSection was not found in kernel32.dll. Apparently this was added in Windows 98, but Windows 95 only has EnterCriticalSection – meaning there is no non-blocking way to try to acquire a lock. As a quick and dirty hack, I just used EnterCriticalSection and indeed, now it would start – and work! Obviously, that is not a real solution, and it turns out that even on later versions of the Windows 9x family, CRITICAL_SECTION does not fully work. So I ended up falling back to CreateMutex and WaitForSingleObject if Windows 9x is detected – or if TryEnterCriticalSection is not found, which turns out to be also missing in NT versions before 4.0 – though I did not test it on Windows NT 3.51 yet.
🌐 Commit “Avoid CRITICAL_SECTION on Windows 9x and NT < 4”

So now I have the tests starting and all but one of them succeed (when built with --disable-sockets). But what is the failing test? It turns out the OFModule test is failing to load the test plugin. But why? Well, it turns out Microsoft actually wrote about it in their KB:
🌐 PRB: Calling LoadLibrary() to Load a DLL That Has Static TLS (118816)
But why? ObjFW's configure is disabling compiler TLS for Windows and the TLS API is used instead, so why is it failing to load? Well, it turns out that the MinGW-w64 crt references __dyn_tls_init_callback, and if that symbol is missing, pulls in some more files that contain TLS tables. Simply providing a common __dyn_tls_init_callback symbol avoids that and the plugin loads. Apparently this has been fixed in upstream MinGW-w64, but there is no release yet. So I committed a workaround and will just wait for a new release.
🌐 Commit “Add a common symbol for __dyn_tls_init_callback”

But now we have everything working, right? Well, remember that we used --disable-sockets? It wouldn't be a proper port to Windows 95 if we can't use sockets, right? While we could just install Winsock 2 on Windows 95 and be done, that has the same problem as msvcrt: It's not available for Win32s. Plus, making users install dependencies manually is not great. So we would need to use Winsock 2 if available and otherwise Winsock 1. We could just LoadLibrary ws2_32.dll and failing that LoadLibrary wsock32.dll and get every function via GetProcAddress. But it turns out there is a better way! It turns out Winsock 2 still provides wsock32.dll and just forwards all calls to ws2_32.dll. So we can just link against wsock32.dll and it will work on all versions. But that way we would lose IPv6 support, right? Well, we can hack around that! It turns out that you can include winsock2.h and still link against wsock32.dll. That has the problem that some enums have different values in Winsock 1 and 2, but all the ones being used by ObjFW have the same value in both, so we can just do that.
🌐 Commit “Link wsock32.dll instead of ws2_32.dll”

The only other problem is missing iphlpapi.dll, but we can just load this dynamically, too, and now all tests pass!
🌐 Commit “Don't statically link iphlpapi.dll”
The only problem is that ObjFW cannot obtain the name server on Windows 95, but I'll fix this as a follow up.

And last but not least, here is a screenshot of all tests passing:

I hope that with this blog post, I could also dispel the myth that Windows 95 and Windows 98 are basically the same. A lot of APIs were only added in Windows 98 – and Windows 98 also introduced an entirely new driver model (WDM instead of VxD). And while we're at it: Windows Me is also not just a reskin of Windows 98. It added even more new APIs that were mostly coming from NT (and made USB actually usable).

Edit

Obtaining the DNS server is now also supported on Windows 95 – without iphlpapi.dll, as that is even unavailable on Windows 95 when installing Winsock 2. It now works with both Winsock 1 and Winsock 2 and directly queries the VDHCP.VxD driver. Surprisingly, this method is not documented, nor could I find it anywhere on the internet.
🌐 Commit “OFDNSResolverSettings: Add support for Windows 95”
